titleEn: Australian classrooms are getting a ‘digital detox’ – what does this mean for schools and students?
titleZh: 澳大利亚课堂的“数字排毒”，对师生意味着什么？
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: The federal government is pushing for a “digital detox” in schools.
paragraphs.zh: 联邦政府正在推动学校进行“数字排毒”。

paragraphs.en: In a new report, it outlines growing concerns about the use of digital technologies in classrooms. This includes concerns about artificial intelligence (AI) harming children’s critical thinking, concentration and problem-solving skills.
paragraphs.zh: 在一份新的报告中，该组织概述了人们对数字技术在课堂上的使用日益担忧。其中包括对人工智能（AI）损害儿童批判性思维、注意力和解决问题能力的担忧。

paragraphs.en: The government now plans to reduce the time students spend on screens and limit AI use at school to improve learning. Education Minister Jason Clare told ABC Radio National on Thursday,
paragraphs.zh: 政府现在计划减少学生花在屏幕上的时间，并限制AI在学校的使用，以提高学习效果。教育部长贾森克莱尔周四告诉美国广播公司全国广播电台，

paragraphs.en: I’m not making the argument here to burn the iPads […] but I am saying that there’s a pretty good argument here for more pen and paper and less tech.
paragraphs.zh: 我不是在这里提出烧掉iPad的论点[...]，但我是说，这里有一个很好的论点，更多的笔和纸，少科技。

paragraphs.en: This position reverses a decades-long trend of expanding the use of digital technologies in Australian classrooms.
paragraphs.zh: 这一立场扭转了澳大利亚数十年来在课堂上扩大数字技术使用的趋势。

paragraphs.en: What does this report mean for schools? And what’s missing in our discussion about screens in schools so far?
paragraphs.zh: 这份报告对学校意味着什么？到目前为止，在我们关于学校屏幕的讨论中还缺少什么？

paragraphs.en: What’s in the report?
paragraphs.zh: 报告里写了什么？

paragraphs.en: State and federal education ministers have agreed to consider national limits on screen use. This builds on screen-time limits already flagged in New South Wales and Victoria and soon to be piloted in Western Australia. It also follows international examples such as Norway and New York.
paragraphs.zh: 各州和联邦教育部长已同意考虑在全国范围内限制屏幕使用。新南威尔士州和维多利亚州已经明确规定了屏幕使用时间限制，不久将在西澳大利亚州试行。该计划还将效仿挪威和纽约州等国际国家的做法。

paragraphs.en: The report also flags:
paragraphs.zh: 该报告还标记：

paragraphs.en: some of the Year 5 NAPLAN tests will return to a written assessment (it is currently all done online)
paragraphs.zh: 一些第5年的NAPLAN测试将返回书面评估（目前全部在线完成）

paragraphs.en: a new taskforce to look at “digital detoxing” in schools, set to report to ministers three times next year, and
paragraphs.zh: 一个新的工作组来研究学校的“数字解毒”，明年将向部长们报告三次，以及

paragraphs.en: generative AI to be restricted in primary schools and for high school assessments.
paragraphs.zh: 生成性人工智能将被限制在小学和高中评估中。

paragraphs.en: The argument for making these changes is that educational technology should be used to support effective teaching, but not replace it. The report says,
paragraphs.zh: 做出这些改变的理由是教育技术应该用来支持有效的教学，而不是取代它。

paragraphs.en: when technology is used, it should be for a purpose, including supporting student learning and wellbeing, and if it causes harm, it should be restricted.
paragraphs.zh: 当技术被使用时，它应该是有目的的，包括支持学生的学习和福利，如果它造成伤害，它应该受到限制。

paragraphs.en: What does this mean for schools?
paragraphs.zh: 这对学校意味着什么？

paragraphs.en: In practical terms, these changes will mean less emphasis on technology, with a return to pens and paper. And teachers will increasingly have hard limits on the amount of time they can use technology in lessons, particularly in primary schools.
paragraphs.zh: 实际上，这些变化将意味着不再那么强调技术，而是回归纸笔。教师在课堂上使用技术的时间将越来越受到严格的限制，尤其是在小学。

paragraphs.en: For some teachers, this may require a complete revamp of their teaching practices. For others, there may be no noticeable difference as they are not using technology much currently.
paragraphs.zh: 对于一些教师来说，这可能需要他们的教学实践进行彻底的改革。对于其他教师来说，由于他们目前没有太多地使用科技，可能没有明显的区别。

paragraphs.en: There is no comprehensive national data on how much time Australian children spend on devices at school.
paragraphs.zh: 目前还没有关于澳大利亚儿童在学校花多少时间在设备上的全面的全国数据。

paragraphs.en: The rules around tech use have been just as patchy. For example, phone bans are implemented at state level. Almost everything else has been decided school by school, including whether students bring a laptop and which AI tools they can use.
paragraphs.zh: 科技使用方面的规定也同样不完善。例如，电话禁令是在州一级实施的。几乎所有其他事情都是由学校决定的，包括学生是否携带笔记本电脑，以及他们可以使用哪些AI工具。

paragraphs.en: What does the research say?
paragraphs.zh: 研究结果如何？

paragraphs.en: The evidence around how much technology is optimal for learning is also mixed.
paragraphs.zh: 关于多少技术对学习是最佳的证据也是喜忧参半。

paragraphs.en: Recent international test results suggest 15-year-old students who use devices moderately for learning do better than both heavy users and non-users. But given so few students now go without technology, critics argue the comparison with non-users does not tell us anything particularly useful.
paragraphs.zh: 最近的国际测试结果显示，适度使用电子设备学习的15岁学生比重度使用者和非使用者的成绩都要好。但鉴于现在没有科技设备的学生如此之少，批评人士认为，与非使用者的比较并没有告诉我们任何特别有用的东西。

paragraphs.en: Research also suggests raising the bar for the use of educational technologies (which most of the time means screens) makes sense. For decades, we have lacked sufficient evidence of their positive impact on learning.
paragraphs.zh: 研究还表明，提高教育技术（大多数时候指的是屏幕）的使用门槛是有道理的。几十年来，我们一直缺乏足够的证据证明它们对学习的积极影响。

paragraphs.en: For example, a 2015 OECD analysis found countries that had invested heavily in computers for schools saw no appreciable improvement in students’ reading, maths or science scores.
paragraphs.zh: 例如，经合组织2015年的一项分析发现，那些在学校电脑上投入巨资的国家，学生的阅读、数学或科学成绩没有明显改善。

paragraphs.en: Tech can help, but …
paragraphs.zh: 技术可以帮上忙，但是...

paragraphs.en: That isn’t to say technology never helps. Used for something specific, such as more targeted practice or more precise feedback, it can improve learning.
paragraphs.zh: 这并不是说技术永远不会有帮助。用于特定的事情，例如更有针对性的练习或更精确的反馈，它可以改善学习。

paragraphs.en: But there has not been enough onus on those selling technologies to schools to demonstrate their positive impact on learning. Instead, implementation decisions are often made on the basis of pilots and word of mouth.
paragraphs.zh: 但是，向学校出售技术的人没有足够的责任来证明它们对学习的积极影响。相反，实施决策往往是根据试点和口碑做出的。

paragraphs.en: And with the introduction of generative AI and AI agents, concerns have moved beyond a lack of evidence around the positive impact of technology on learning to a concern about negative impacts.
paragraphs.zh: 随着生成人工智能和人工智能代理的引入，人们的担忧已经从缺乏证据证明技术对学习的积极影响转变为对负面影响的担忧。

paragraphs.en: Discussions about students using AI to offload their learning have dominated global conversations in education. The main concern is AI use will lead to “cognitive stunting”, where repeated use of the technology can weaken learning and thinking skills.
paragraphs.zh: 关于学生使用人工智能来减轻学习负担的讨论主导了全球教育对话。主要担忧是人工智能的使用将导致“认知发育迟缓”，即重复使用该技术会削弱学习和思考能力。

paragraphs.en: UNESCO has published arguments that “cognitive friction” – or struggle – is where real learning happens. In September, at a global meeting, education ministers called for AI that makes learners reason and do the “hard thinking” work themselves.
paragraphs.zh: 联合国教科文组织（UNESCO）曾发表文章称，“认知摩擦”--或称挣扎--是真实的学习发生的地方。今年9月，在一次全球会议上，教育部长们呼吁人工智能让学习者自己进行推理和“艰苦的思考”。

paragraphs.en: What next?
paragraphs.zh: 接下来呢？

paragraphs.en: But while this latest report is a step in the right direction, we need more planning and more information.
paragraphs.zh: 但是，虽然这份最新报告是朝着正确方向迈出的一步，但我们需要更多的规划和更多的信息。

paragraphs.en: Whether we like it or not, technology (including AI) is increasingly part of the world young people live in and will work in. It’s now almost unavoidable if you use Google, for example.
paragraphs.zh: 无论我们喜欢与否，技术（包括人工智能）越来越多地成为年轻人生活和工作的世界的一部分。

paragraphs.en: One of the major questions the new taskforce will need to address is: when are the appropriate times and circumstances to integrate technologies into classrooms?
paragraphs.zh: 新工作组需要解决的一个主要问题是：什么时候是将技术融入课堂的适当时机和环境？

paragraphs.en: Students will increasingly be interacting with technologies such as AI as soon as they walk out of the school gates (if they aren’t already). Preparing them to survive and thrive in this new era of AI is an important job for schools.
paragraphs.zh: 学生们一走出校门就会越来越多地与人工智能等技术进行互动（如果他们还没有的话）。让他们在这个人工智能的新时代做好生存和发展的准备是学校的一项重要工作。

paragraphs.en: A complete technology ban across all of primary and secondary schooling is not what is being suggested by the government. So, questions about how and when remain open.
paragraphs.zh: 政府并没有建议在中小学全面禁止使用高科技产品。因此，关于如何以及何时禁止的问题仍然悬而未决。

paragraphs.en: We need to do a lot more research and thinking to truly ensure our education and training systems are appropriate for the age of AI.
paragraphs.zh: 我们需要做更多的研究和思考，以真正确保我们的教育和培训系统适合人工智能时代。

paragraphs.en: As world leaders Singapore and Estonia have shown, this will require investing in teachers and using tools designed for learning, rather than just churning out answers.
paragraphs.zh: 正如世界领导人新加坡和爱沙尼亚所表明的那样，这将需要投资于教师和使用为学习而设计的工具，而不仅仅是炮制答案。
